newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended weaker following noticeable declines in New York. December fell through support at $328.00 to close $2.80 lower at $327.50. March shed $3.10 to close at $327. In New York raw sugar futures closed sharply lower. Abundant supplies, especially from Brazil, and weak end-user demand contributed to the fall. Even though last week's flurry of liquidation reduced open interest in October, the speculative long position remains high, which points to further downward pressure. Open interest stood at 24,128 off 1,919 in October, while open interest in the March contract stood at 67,745 up 215 lots.

EUROPE - Light rains covered the southern half of Europe during the week ended September 24. The northern areas, including most of the UK, Germany and Poland were mostly dry. The very heavy rains in the eastern half of the continent finally came to an end but the area is still reporting 150 to 350 per cent of normal rainfall for the month to date. The rains not only affected sugar content, but also hampered harvesting operations. Further rains are forecast, which will not alleviate the situation. There were also heavy rains in the former Soviet Union. Rain receipts were two to four times the normal for the month of September. Additional rains are expected which will make harvesting extremely difficult. Moreover, the later the harvest, the greater the danger of an early frost, which could lead to noticeable losses.

DENMARK - Sugar exports in June 1996 amounted to 14,358 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 20,111 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first nine months of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 121,543 tonnes, down from last year's 155,122 tonnes. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 199,559 tonnes against 255,177 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/June 1995/96 were Norway with 86,187 tonnes whites compared to 81,635 tonnes and Iceland with 6,637 tonnes against 6,484 tonnes. Sugar imports in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) reached 9,196 tonnes, up from last year's 3,283 tonnes. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 4,960 tonnes against 8,598 tonnes in 1993/94. The major country of origin in October/June 1995/96 was Germany with 7,540 tonnes whites against 2,360 tonnes.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports from third countries in July 1996 amounted to 102,066 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 1.05 million tonnes, down from 1.11 million tonnes imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports from third countries in October/September 1994/95 reached 1.36 million tonnes. Major countries of origin in October/July 1995/96 were Mauritius with 374,716 tonnes raws against 360,579 tonnes, Fiji with 165,080 tonnes against 134,500 tonnes, Guyana with 134,296 tonnes compared to 136,400 tonnes and Jamaica with 125,227 tonnes against 126,300 tonnes. Sugar exports to third countries in July 1996 amounted to 29,471 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in October/July 1995/96 up to 271,361 tonnes, sharply down from the previous year's 400,688 tonnes. Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Israel with 103,808 tonnes whites against 118,440 tonnes, Norway with 38,440 tonnes compared to 31,669 tonnes and Turkey with 18,664 tonnes against 2,113 tonnes.

CANADA - Sugar imports in June 1996 dropped to 13,351 tonnes, raw value, down from 166,746 tonnes in May 1996 and 111,875 tonnes in June 1995. However, cumulative imports in 1995/96 (October/June) amounted to 843,980 tonnes, considerably up on the previous year's 797,882 tonnes. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 1.01 million tonnes, down from 1.21 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/June 1995/96 were Australia with 504,229 tonnes raws against 451,957 tonnes, Cuba with 117,743 tonnes, up from last year's 75,809 tonnes and Colombia with 57,361 tonnes against nil.
